```{r Location}
#1. Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

#2. Read in your data
df <- read.csv("RPM_Region_Ben.csv", header = TRUE)

#3. Pivot from wide to long format
df_long <- df %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = astroviridae:spinaeroviridae
,  # adjust if other viral families are included
    names_to = "Viral_Family",
    values_to = "RPM"
  )

df_grouped <- df_long %>%
  group_by(Location, Viral_Family) %>%
  summarise(Total_RPM = sum(RPM), .groups = "drop")

#4. Plot: Stacked bar plot
ggplot(df_grouped, aes(x = Location, y = Total_RPM, fill = Viral_Family)) +
  geom_bar(position="fill", stat = "identity") +
  labs(x = "Location", y = "Total Reads Per Million", fill = "Viral Family") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5))


# Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Step 1: Read the data
df <- read.csv("RPM_Region_Ben.csv", header = TRUE)

# Step 2: Pivot to long format (viral families into rows)
df_long <- df %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = astroviridae:spinaeroviridae,
    names_to = "Viral_Family",
    values_to = "RPM"
  )

# Step 3: Summarise RPM per sample type and viral family
df_summary <- df_long %>%
  group_by(Location, Viral_Family) %>%
  summarise(Total_RPM = sum(RPM), .groups = "drop")

# Step 4: Plot pie chart for each sample type
ggplot(df_summary, aes(x = 1, y = Total_RPM, fill = Viral_Family)) +
  geom_bar(position="fill", stat = "identity", width = 1) +
  coord_polar("y") +
  facet_wrap(~ Location) +
  labs(title = "Viral Family Composition by Location",
       y = "", x = "", fill = "Viral Family") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

```

```{r health status}
# Load required libraries-Pie chart NO SEDOREOVIRIDAE,PICORNA,Param
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Step 1: Read the data
df <- read.csv("RPM_HS_Ben.csv", header = TRUE)

# Step 2: Pivot to long format (viral families into rows)
df_long <- df %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(astroviridae,caliciviridae,coronaviridae,nodaviridae,phenuviridae,spinaeroviridae),
    names_to = "Viral_Family",
    values_to = "RPM"
  )

# Step 3: Summarise RPM per sample type and viral family
# AND calculate percentage
df_summary <- df_long %>%
  group_by(Health_status, Viral_Family) %>%
  summarise(Total_RPM = sum(RPM), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(Health_status) %>%
  mutate(Percentage = Total_RPM / sum(Total_RPM) * 100) %>%
  ungroup()

# Step 4: Plot pie chart for each sample type + add percentages
ggplot(df_summary, aes(x = 1, y = Total_RPM, fill = Viral_Family)) +
  geom_bar(position="fill", stat = "identity", width = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(Percentage, 1), "%")),
  position = position_fill(vjust = 0.5), color = "black", size = 3) + 
  coord_polar("y") +
  facet_wrap(~ Health_status) +
  labs(title = "Viral Family Composition by Health Status",
       y = "", x = "", fill = "Viral Family") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```

```{r Normalised viral abundance by General_Location Seal}
# Load libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)

# Step 1: Load normalised abundance data
normalised_raw <- read.csv("Normalised_LID_Ben.csv", header = TRUE, row.names = 1)

# Step 2: Transpose so families are rows, libraries are columns
normalised <- t(normalised_raw)

# Step 3: Convert to data frame
normalised_df <- as.data.frame(normalised)

# Step 4: Add viral family as a column
normalised_df$family <- rownames(normalised_df)

# Step 5: Reshape to long format
melted <- melt(normalised_df, id.vars = "family", variable.name = "library", value.name = "abundance")

# Step 6: Load library metadata (e.g. from RPM_Order.csv)
metadata <- read.csv("RPM_Meta_Ben.csv", header = TRUE)
names(metadata)

# Step 7: Merge metadata with melted data
melted$library <- as.character(melted$library)
metadata$Library_ID <- as.character(metadata$Library_ID)

merged <- left_join(melted, metadata, by = c("library" = "Library_ID"))

# Step 8: Create unique label using General_Location, Bird_order, Bird_species, and library ID
merged <- merged %>%
  mutate(library_label = paste(Location, Health_status, library, sep = " | "))

# Step 9: Order factor levels by Location > Health_status 
merged$Location <- factor(merged$Location,levels = c("Cape Foulwind","Cape Palliser","Cape Saunders","Kaikoura Ohau","Kaikoura Peninsula","Kaikoura South Coast","OPERA"))
merged$Health_status <- factor(merged$Health_status,levels = c("Diseased", "Healthy"))
 
merged$library_label <- factor(
  merged$library_label,
  levels = merged %>%
    distinct(library, library_label, Location, Health_status) %>%
    arrange(Location, Health_status, library) %>%
    pull(library_label))
  
# Step 10: Plot
ggplot(merged, aes(x = library_label, y = family, fill = abundance+1e-6)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "blue", trans = "log10") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Library (Grouped by Region and Health Status)", y = "Viral Family", fill = "Normalised Abundance") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8))

write.csv(merged, "merged_data_heatmap_ordered_Ben.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```

```{r Shannon, location}
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr) 
library(ggplot2) 
library(vegan) # For diversity() function 
library(rstatix) # For Dunn's test 
library(ggpubr) # For adding P-values to plots

# Read in your data
data_seal <- read.csv("RPM_Region_Ben.csv", header = TRUE)

# Step 1: Identify viral family columns
viral_cols <- which(names(data_seal) %in% c("astroviridae", "caliciviridae",
 "coronaviridae", "nodaviridae",
 "paramyxoviridae", "phenuviridae", "picornaviridae", 
 "sedoreoviridae", "spinaeroviridae"))

names(data_seal)[viral_cols]
length(viral_cols)

# Step 2: Calculate Shannon index per sample
# vegan::diversity requires non-negative abundance values
str(data_seal[, viral_cols])
names(data_seal)

data_seal$shannon <- diversity(data_seal[, viral_cols], index = "shannon")

# Step 3: Summarize Shannon index by Bird_order
order_summary <- data_seal %>%
  group_by(Location) %>%
  summarise(mean_shannon = mean(shannon),
            sd_shannon = sd(shannon),
            n = n(),
            se_shannon = sd_shannon / sqrt(n))

# View summary table
print(order_summary)

# Step 4: Plot Shannon index per Location
ggplot(data_seal, aes(x = Location, y = shannon)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "skyblue", color = "black") +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, height = 0, alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Shannon Diversity Index per Location",
       y = "Shannon Diversity (H')",
       x = "Location") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# Step 5: Kruskal-Wallis test for Shannon index
kruskal.test(shannon ~ Location, data = data_seal)
#Kruskal-Wallis chi-squared = 5.8862, df = 6, p-value = 0.4361

```

```{r Shannon, region}
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr) 
library(ggplot2) 
library(vegan) # For diversity() function 
library(rstatix) # For Dunn's test 
library(ggpubr) # For adding P-values to plots
# Read in your data
data_seal2 <- read.csv("RPM_Broadregion_Ben.csv", header = TRUE)

# Step 1: Identify viral family columns
viral_cols <- which(names(data_seal2) %in% c("astroviridae", "caliciviridae",
 "coronaviridae", "nodaviridae",
 "paramyxoviridae", "phenuviridae", "picornaviridae", 
 "sedoreoviridae", "spinaeroviridae"))

names(data_seal2)[viral_cols]
length(viral_cols)

# Step 2: Calculate Shannon index per sample
# vegan::diversity requires non-negative abundance values
str(data_seal2[, viral_cols])
names(data_seal2)

data_seal2$shannon <- diversity(data_seal2[, viral_cols], index = "shannon")

# Step 3: Summarize Shannon index by Bird_order
order_summary <- data_seal2 %>%
  group_by(Location) %>%
  summarise(mean_shannon = mean(shannon),
            sd_shannon = sd(shannon),
            n = n(),
            se_shannon = sd_shannon / sqrt(n))

# View summary table
print(order_summary)

# Step 4: Plot Shannon index per Location
ggplot(data_seal2, aes(x = Location, y = shannon)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "skyblue", color = "black") +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, height = 0, alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Shannon Diversity Index by Region",
       y = "Shannon Diversity (H')",
       x = "Location") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# Step 5: Kruskal-Wallis test for Shannon index
kruskal.test(shannon ~ Location, data = data_seal2)
#Kruskal-Wallis chi-squared = 4.0208, df = 3, p-value = 0.2592

# Step 5.5: Pairwise Dunn's test # 
pairwise_results <- data_seal2 %>% dunn_test( shannon ~ Location, p.adjust.method = "BH" ) 

# View all pairwise results 
print(pairwise_results) 

# Step 6: Create a clean table of pairwise P-values
pairwise_table <- pairwise_results %>% select(group1, group2, p, p.adj, p.adj.signif) 
print(pairwise_table) 

# Prepare P-value labels
# ---------------------------------------------------------

pairwise_results <- pairwise_results %>%
  mutate(
    p.label = paste0(
      "P = ",
      format.pval(p.adj, digits = 3, eps = 0.001)
    )
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Set positions for the six P-value brackets
# ---------------------------------------------------------

pairwise_results <- pairwise_results %>%
  mutate(
    y.position = case_when(

      # Adjacent comparisons
      group1 == "Dunedin" &
        group2 == "Kaikoura" ~ 1.08,

      group1 == "Kaikoura" &
        group2 == "Wairarapa" ~ 1.18,

      group1 == "Wairarapa" &
        group2 == "Westport" ~ 1.28,

      # Comparisons spanning two locations
      group1 == "Dunedin" &
        group2 == "Wairarapa" ~ 1.38,

      group1 == "Kaikoura" &
        group2 == "Westport" ~ 1.48,

      # Largest comparison
      group1 == "Dunedin" &
        group2 == "Westport" ~ 1.58
    )
  )


# Check that all six comparisons have a position
print(
  pairwise_results %>%
    select(group1, group2, p.label, y.position)
)


# Final plot
# ---------------------------------------------------------

ggplot(data_seal2, aes(x = Location, y = shannon)) +

  geom_boxplot(
    fill = "skyblue",
    color = "black",
    width = 0.6
  ) +

  geom_jitter(
    width = 0.15,
    height = 0,
    alpha = 0.5,
    size = 2
  ) +

  stat_pvalue_manual(
    pairwise_results,
    label = "p.label",
    xmin = "group1",
    xmax = "group2",
    y.position = "y.position",
    tip.length = 0.01,
    bracket.size = 0.4
  ) +

  labs(
    y = "Shannon Diversity (H')",
    x = "Location"
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_blank(),

    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1,
      color = "black"
    ),

    axis.text.y = element_text(
      color = "black"
    ),

    axis.title = element_text(
      color = "black"
    ),

    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),

    plot.margin = margin(
      t = 10,
      r = 20,
      b = 20,
      l = 20
    )
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.02))
  ) +

  coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(0, 1.65),
    clip = "off"
  )
```

```{r NMDS on virome composition by location}
# Load required packages
library(vegan)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)

# Step 1: Load the data
df <- read_csv("RPM_Region_Ben.csv")

# Step 2: Remove library 33 (currently ignored)
# df <- df %>% filter(Bird_lib != 33)

# Step 3: Subset the viral abundance data
viral_data <- df %>% select(astroviridae:spinaeroviridae)

# Step 4: Filter out samples with all zeros
non_zero_rows <- rowSums(viral_data) > 0
df_filtered <- df[non_zero_rows, ]
viral_data_filtered <- viral_data[non_zero_rows, ]

# Step 5: Create Bray-Curtis distance matrix
bray_dist <- vegdist(viral_data_filtered, method = "bray")

# Step 6: Run NMDS
set.seed(123)  # for reproducibility
nmds <- metaMDS(viral_data_filtered, distance = "bray", k = 2)
nmds$stress
# Step 7: Plot stress plot (optional)
stressplot(nmds)

# Step 8: Combine NMDS points with metadata
mds_points <- as.data.frame(nmds$points)
mds_combined <- cbind(mds_points, Location = df_filtered$Location)

# Step 9: NMDS plot coloured by bird order
ggplot(mds_combined, aes(x = MDS1, y = MDS2, color = Location)) +
  geom_jitter(size = 3, width = 0.1, height = 0.1) +  # Add jitter
  stat_ellipse(type = "t", linetype = "dashed", size = 1) +
  labs(title = "NMDS of Viral Communities by Location",
       x = "NMDS1", y = "NMDS2") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.title = element_blank())

# Step 10: PERMANOVA testing effect of bird order on beta diversity
set.seed(123)
adonis_result <- adonis2(bray_dist ~ Location, data = df_filtered, permutations = 999)

# Step 11: Print result
print(adonis_result)

#          Df SumOfSqs      R2      F Pr(>F)    
#Model      6   3.3878 0.41006 1.7377  0.005 **

#2nd test - google: dont use location

```

```{r NMDS on virome composition by Region}
# Step 10: PERMANOVA testing effect of bird order on beta diversity
set.seed(123)
adonis_result <- adonis2(bray_dist ~ Location, data = df_filtered, permutations = 999)

# Step 11: Print result
print(adonis_result)

#          Df SumOfSqs      R2      F Pr(>F)    
#Model      3   2.1236 0.25705 2.0759  0.004 **
#second test here: pairwise adonis

# Step 12: Pairwise PERMANOVA between Locations

# Get the unique Location groups
locations <- unique(df_filtered$Location)

# Create all pairwise combinations
location_pairs <- combn(locations, 2, simplify = FALSE)

# Run PERMANOVA for each pair
pairwise_results <- lapply(location_pairs, function(pair) {
  
  # Keep only the two Locations being compared
  keep <- df_filtered$Location %in% pair
  
  # Subset distance matrix
  dist_subset <- as.dist(as.matrix(bray_dist)[keep, keep])
  
  # Subset metadata
  data_subset <- df_filtered[keep, ]
  
  # Run PERMANOVA
  result <- adonis2(
    dist_subset ~ Location,
    data = data_subset,
    permutations = 999
  )
  
  # Return results
  data.frame(
    Location_1 = pair[1],
    Location_2 = pair[2],
    F = result$F[1],
    R2 = result$R2[1],
    p_value = result$`Pr(>F)`[1]
  )
})

# Combine results into one table
pairwise_results <- bind_rows(pairwise_results)

# Correct for multiple comparisons
pairwise_results$p_adjusted <- p.adjust(
  pairwise_results$p_value,
  method = "BH"
)

# View results
pairwise_results
```

```{r Shannon, region-NOSEDO}
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr) 
library(ggplot2) 
library(vegan) # For diversity() function 
library(rstatix) # For Dunn's test 
library(ggpubr) # For adding P-values to plots
# Read in your data
data_seal2 <- read.csv("RPM_Broadregion_Ben.csv", header = TRUE)

# Step 1: Identify viral family columns
viral_cols <- which(names(data_seal2) %in% c("astroviridae", "caliciviridae",
 "coronaviridae", "nodaviridae",
 "paramyxoviridae", "phenuviridae", "picornaviridae", "spinaeroviridae"))

names(data_seal2)[viral_cols]
length(viral_cols)

# Step 2: Calculate Shannon index per sample
# vegan::diversity requires non-negative abundance values
str(data_seal2[, viral_cols])
names(data_seal2)

data_seal2$shannon <- diversity(data_seal2[, viral_cols], index = "shannon")

# Step 3: Summarize Shannon index by Bird_order
order_summary <- data_seal2 %>%
  group_by(Location) %>%
  summarise(mean_shannon = mean(shannon),
            sd_shannon = sd(shannon),
            n = n(),
            se_shannon = sd_shannon / sqrt(n))

# View summary table
print(order_summary)

# Step 4: Plot Shannon index per Location
ggplot(data_seal2, aes(x = Location, y = shannon)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "skyblue", color = "black") +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, height = 0, alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Shannon Diversity Index by Region",
       y = "Shannon Diversity (H')",
       x = "Location") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# Step 5: Kruskal-Wallis test for Shannon index
kruskal.test(shannon ~ Location, data = data_seal2)
#Kruskal-Wallis chi-squared = 3.4731, df = 3, p-value = 0.3243

table(data_seal3$Health_status)

# Step 5.5: Pairwise Dunn's test # 
pairwise_results <- data_seal2 %>% dunn_test( shannon ~ Location, p.adjust.method = "BH" ) 

# View all pairwise results 
print(pairwise_results) 

# Step 6: Create a clean table of pairwise P-values
pairwise_table <- pairwise_results %>% select(group1, group2, p, p.adj, p.adj.signif) 
print(pairwise_table) 

# Prepare P-value labels
# ---------------------------------------------------------

pairwise_results <- pairwise_results %>%
  mutate(
    p.label = paste0(
      "P = ",
      format.pval(p.adj, digits = 3, eps = 0.001)
    )
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Set positions for the six P-value brackets
# ---------------------------------------------------------

pairwise_results <- pairwise_results %>%
  mutate(
    y.position = case_when(

      # Adjacent comparisons
      group1 == "Dunedin" &
        group2 == "Kaikoura" ~ 1.08,

      group1 == "Kaikoura" &
        group2 == "Wairarapa" ~ 1.18,

      group1 == "Wairarapa" &
        group2 == "Westport" ~ 1.28,

      # Comparisons spanning two locations
      group1 == "Dunedin" &
        group2 == "Wairarapa" ~ 1.38,

      group1 == "Kaikoura" &
        group2 == "Westport" ~ 1.48,

      # Largest comparison
      group1 == "Dunedin" &
        group2 == "Westport" ~ 1.58
    )
  )


# Check that all six comparisons have a position
print(
  pairwise_results %>%
    select(group1, group2, p.label, y.position)
)


# Final plot
# ---------------------------------------------------------

ggplot(data_seal2, aes(x = Location, y = shannon)) +

  geom_boxplot(
    fill = "skyblue",
    color = "black",
    width = 0.6
  ) +

  geom_jitter(
    width = 0.15,
    height = 0,
    alpha = 0.5,
    size = 2
  ) +

  stat_pvalue_manual(
    pairwise_results,
    label = "p.label",
    xmin = "group1",
    xmax = "group2",
    y.position = "y.position",
    tip.length = 0.01,
    bracket.size = 0.4
  ) +

  labs(
    y = "Shannon Diversity (H')",
    x = "Location"
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_blank(),

    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1,
      color = "black"
    ),

    axis.text.y = element_text(
      color = "black"
    ),

    axis.title = element_text(
      color = "black"
    ),

    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),

    plot.margin = margin(
      t = 10,
      r = 20,
      b = 20,
      l = 20
    )
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.02))
  ) +

  coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(0, 1.65),
    clip = "off"
  )
```
